title: Hotteok Brown-Sugar Seed Pancakes
shortDescription: Soft yeasted wheat dough encloses brown sugar, cinnamon, sunflower seed, pumpkin seed, and sesame filling, then pan-fries into crisp-edged pancakes with molten centers.
culturalContext: Hotteok is a Korean filled pancake strongly associated with street snacks and cool-weather eating. Fillings and dough styles have changed over time and may include nuts, seeds, or savory ingredients; this draft uses a clearly labeled seed filling.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Heavy nonstick or well-seasoned skillet with lid
Flat hotteok press or oiled metal spatula

ingredients.preparation: spooned and leveled if measured by volume

instructions.heading: Mix the dough
instructions.action: Combine warm water, yeast, and dough sugar. Add flour, salt, and 1 tablespoon oil; stir with a clean spoon until no dry flour remains and a very sticky dough forms.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Dough is sticky, shaggy, and fully hydrated with no flour pockets.
instructions.safetyNote: Raw flour can contain harmful germs; do not taste raw dough and wash hands and surfaces after flour contact.

instructions.heading: Let the dough rise
instructions.action: Cover and rise in a draft-free place for about 1 hour, until visibly doubled and bubbly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Dough has doubled and shows bubbles across the surface.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean food-safe cover and do not place the bowl near raw foods or excessive heat.

instructions.heading: Prepare the filling
instructions.action: Mix brown sugar, chopped sunflower and pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, and cinnamon. Divide mentally or by weight into 8 equal portions.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Seeds are fine enough not to puncture the dough and the mixture is evenly speckled.
instructions.safetyNote: Check seed packages for sesame, peanut, and tree-nut facility cross-contact before serving guests.

instructions.heading: Fill the pancakes
instructions.action: Oil hands lightly, deflate the dough, and divide into 8 pieces. Flatten one piece in an oiled palm, add about 2 tablespoons filling, gather edges over it, and pinch firmly closed; repeat.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Each ball is fully sealed with no sugar visible through the seam.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw dough away from ready-to-eat foods and clean flour residue before cooking begins.

instructions.heading: Pan-fry and press
instructions.action: Heat a thin film of oil over medium-low. Place 2 pancakes seam-side down, cook 1 minute, turn, then press gently to 10 cm / 4 inches. Cover and cook 2 minutes; uncover, turn, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more. Repeat with fresh oil as needed.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Both sides are deep golden, the dough edge looks cooked rather than wet, and no raw seam remains.
instructions.safetyNote: Molten sugar can cause severe burns; press gradually, keep seams intact, and never touch leaked filling.

instructions.heading: Cool before eating
instructions.action: Transfer to a wire rack and cool at least 15 minutes before serving.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Pancakes remain warm but can be held comfortably; filling has thickened slightly.
instructions.safetyNote: Warn diners that the center may remain much hotter than the exterior and supervise children.

grillSetup: No grill is used; cook in a stable heavy skillet on a controlled stovetop burner with a lid and a clear, dry work area.
visualDonenessCues: Dough doubles and becomes bubbly before shaping
Both pancake sides are deep golden
Edges and seams show no wet raw dough
foodSafetyNotes: Do not taste raw flour or raw dough; wash hands and surfaces after flour contact.
Check sesame and seed packages for allergen and facility cross-contact statements.
Keep water away from the hot oil and wipe spills before heating.
Treat leaked brown-sugar filling as a burn hazard.
Cool at least 15 minutes and warn that centers stay hotter than the exterior.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains wheat/gluten and sesame. Seed products may share facilities with peanuts or tree nuts; verify every package and use clean equipment.

substitutions: A nut-free claim requires verified seed packaging and facility information, not only omission of nuts.
Do not substitute gluten-free flour without separately developing dough hydration and structure.
ingredientSourcing: Choose fresh instant yeast and record its expiration date for test-kitchen repeatability.
Source seeds with clear allergen and shared-facility statements.
makeAhead: Mix the filling up to 3 days ahead and keep airtight. This draft does not approve overnight dough fermentation until test-kitchen and safety review.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in a single layer or separated by parchment for up to 3 days; this limit requires food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat in a covered dry skillet over low heat, then uncover to re-crisp. Cool briefly because the sugar center becomes extremely hot again.
leftovers: Freeze cooled pancakes individually for up to 1 month as a quality guideline pending review; thaw under refrigeration before reheating.
servingSuggestions: Serve warm only after the molten center has cooled safely
Offer one pancake per person after a savory meal

faq.question: Why cook hotteok over medium-low heat?
faq.answer: Moderate heat gives the yeasted dough time to cook through before the outside burns and the sugar leaks.

faq.question: When is hotteok safe to bite?
faq.answer: Wait at least 15 minutes and test cautiously; the syrup center can remain dangerously hotter than the crust.
